title: Turkish Get-Up
summary: A slow move from lying to standing with a bell held overhead, for shoulder stability and trunk control rather than muscle size.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.5 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for obliques (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly obliques total.
Library rating 0.4 for abs (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly abs total.
Library rating 0.4 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.3 for quads (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.2 for triceps: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly triceps total.

setup.text: Lie with the bell pressed up over one shoulder.
Roll to your elbow, then your hand, and lift your hips.
Sweep your leg under you, kneel, then stand, keeping the bell over your shoulder.
Reverse the steps to lie back down.

form_cues.cue: Keep your eyes on the bell
Keep your eyes on the bell and move slowly.

mistakes.text: Rushing the steps and losing a vertical arm.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Both sides together, Less systemic fatigue, Easier to learn.
Swap sheet: More stable, Both sides together, Less systemic fatigue.
Swap sheet: Better isolation, More stable, Both sides together.
